compliance.certifications: BSMI, CE, KCC, NRTL, RCM, UKCA, VCCI, TEC, ANATEL, ICASA (data sheet)

environmental.humidity: 5 to 90 percent non-condensing (guide Table 2); the data sheet says 5 to 95 percent
environmental.operating-temp: 0 to 40 C (32 to 104 F); rear-to-front air is subject to 35 C maximum ambient (data sheet note 4)
environmental.storage-temp: -25 to 70 C (guide Table 2); the data sheet says -40 to 70 C

management.console: RJ-45 RS-232 serial on the front, 9600 baud 8N1, no flow control
management.oob: one 10/100/1000 management port on the front
management.usb: one USB port on the front, for software or configuration updates

performance.ports-max-speed: two ports of 400 Gbps; 40 of 100 Gbps; 80 of 50 Gbps; 36 of 40 Gbps; 120 of 25 or 10 Gbps; 24 of 1 Gbps

physical.size-over-ears: 48.3 x 4.4 x 47.2 cm (19 x 1.75 x 18.6 in) with the mounting ears (guide Table 1)
physical.weight: 10.5 kg (23.0 lbs) for the 7280CR3-36S, 7280CR3K-36S and 7280CR3K-36A (guide Table 1, data sheet 10.47 kg)

platform.storage: 8 GB flash (not on the 7280CR3K-36A); SSD 120 GB on the 7280CR3K-36A only

power.power-measure: typical at 25 C ambient with 50 percent load on all ports (data sheet)

thermal.airflow: front-to-rear or rear-to-front, set by the fan modules and supplies fitted

configs.description: The chassis with two AC supplies and two fan modules fitted, front-to-rear air, before any part number: the shape every build below starts from.
configs.name: base

configs.description: Two DC supplies and front-to-rear air: PWR-1011-DC-RED supplies and FAN-7011M-F fan modules. The data sheet lists no DC part number for the switch; the supplies are spares, and a DC build is ordered through the "#" configurable SKUs.
configs.name: dc-f

configs.description: Two DC supplies and rear-to-front air: PWR-1011-DC-BLUE supplies and FAN-7011H-R fan modules. No DC part number is listed for the switch.
configs.name: dc-r

configs.description: The 7280CR3-36S with two AC supplies and front-to-rear air: PWR-1011-AC-RED supplies and FAN-7011M-F fan modules, all with red handles. Ordered as DCS-7280CR3-36S-F.
configs.name: f

configs.description: The 7280CR3K-36A, the K build with an eight-core CPU and a 120 GB SSD, with front-to-rear air. It draws 262 W typical and 437 W maximum (guide Table 4), against 254 W and 423 W for the other builds. Ordered as DCS-7280CR3K-36A-F.
configs.name: k-a-f

configs.description: The 7280CR3K-36A with rear-to-front air, drawing 262 W typical and 437 W maximum. Ordered as DCS-7280CR3K-36A-R.
configs.name: k-a-r

configs.description: The 7280CR3K-36S, the same hardware with the large-routes licence, with front-to-rear air. Ordered as DCS-7280CR3K-36S-F. The data sheet lists no rear-to-front K-36S.
configs.name: k-f

configs.description: The 7280CR3-36S with two AC supplies and rear-to-front air: PWR-1011-AC-BLUE supplies and FAN-7011H-R fan modules, all with blue handles (the data sheet's note 4: 35 C maximum ambient, EOS 4.29.1). Ordered as DCS-7280CR3-36S-R.
configs.name: r

gaps.note: The 7280CR3K-36A draws 262 W typical and 437 W maximum (guide Table 4) against 254 W and 423 W for the other two, has an eight-core CPU in place of a quad-core and carries a 120 GB SSD where the others carry none. No configuration can state a device attribute (the same open gap as cisco/asr-9001). The attrs carry the 7280CR3-36S's figures and the platform lines name all three.

Storage temperature -25 to 70 C (guide Table 2) against -40 to 70 C (data sheet), and relative humidity 5 to 90 percent against 5 to 95 percent. The guide's, the older document by three months, are in attrs.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which is current.

gaps.note: The PWR-1011-DC input is "-40 to -60 VDC, 30 A" in guide Table 3 and "-48 to -60V DC" in the data sheet's power supply table. The guide's is in the component, the data sheet's in its provenance.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which is current.

gaps.note: The data sheet gives 28 QSFP100, 6 QSFP200 and 2 QSFP-DD cages and names no port numbers for any type. Ports 1 to 34 are drawn as ganged QSFP cages and ports 35 and 36 as QSFP-DD; which six of ports 1 to 34 are QSFP200 is not stated, and the group speed is the QSFP100 rate.
gaps.wanted: the guide's or the data sheet's port-to-speed map.

gaps.note: The guide's Figures 3-1 to 3-4 are isometric drawings of another switch and carry no measure, and the kit guides for KIT-7001 and the other spares are not held, so no ear position or rail kit is written.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the mounting bracket position, and the kit guides.

gaps.note: Figure C-5 callout 10 points at a "Port Status LED" the raster does not resolve; guide table 10 describes port LEDs near the ports. No port lamp is modelled.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the lit face, or a larger figure.

gaps.note: The speed strips' legends, the symbols left of the management ports, the symbols under the status lamps and the model line are unreadable or barely readable in the 570 px figure. The lamp symbols are drawn as read; the strips' legends and the port symbols are not drawn.
Which side the latches of the stacked cages face is not visible in the figure. The library's belly-to-belly convention is used (upper cage upright, lower turned 180).
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the stacked cages.

gaps.note: The PWR-1011-DC supplies are drawn as the AC supply's housing with a plain two-pole terminal block. The guide shows a DC supply only in isometric figures; the real terminal arrangement is not drawn.
gaps.wanted: a flat drawing or photograph of the PWR-1011-DC.

gaps.note: The guide's power tables and the data sheet give whole-switch figures only; the fan modules' missing power figure (lint L27) stands. The supplies state their output.
The 1RU grounding point is on the bottom of the chassis for KIT-GND-EXT-1RU (guide section 4.2, Table 5, Figure 4-2). No flat figure measures it, so it is not placed.
gaps.wanted: a flat drawing of the bottom with the grounding bracket holes.

chassis.note: Guide Table 1: 48.3 x 4.4 x 47.2 cm (19 x 1.75 x 18.6 in), 10.5 kg (23.0 lbs), the same for the 7280CR3-36S, 7280CR3K-36S and 7280CR3K-36A. Data sheet: 43.99 x 4.37 x 47.17 cm (17.3 x 1.72 x 18.57 in), 23 lbs (10.47 kg). The width: 48.3 cm is over the mounting ears, so the body between them, which is what is modelled, is the data sheet's 43.99 cm (440.0 here), a 21.5 mm ear each side. The height is the data sheet's 43.7 (the guide rounds it to 4.4 cm). The depth is the data sheet's 471.7 (the guide's 47.2 cm is the same figure rounded). 1RU.

colour.note: The front plate is the 7280CR3-32D4's #aaabad, read there as the median of bare-plate pixels in the guide's figure of the same family.

configurations.note: Data sheet ordering information: DCS-7280CR3-36S-F and -R, DCS-7280CR3K-36S-F (no -R is listed for the K-36S) and DCS-7280CR3K-36A-F and -R ("front to rear air, 2 x AC" and "rear to front air, 2 x AC"). The "#" SKUs ("configurable fans and psu") are orders of parts, not part numbers a DCIM can hold, and are not listed. The data sheet lists no DC build of the switch: the PWR-1011-DC-RED and -BLUE supplies are spares, so the DC configurations are examples with no part number. The K and K-A builds share the base model's size, weight, figure and supplies and differ in memory, CPU, SSD and routes (and, for the 36A, power draw), which a configuration cannot state; each is a configuration with its own part numbers. There is no empty-bay (-S) configuration: the "S" of the model name is not a suffix of this kind and the guide draws no blank for a power supply or fan module.

ears.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide's Chapter 3 mounts the switch with the accessory-kit brackets and shows them in isometric drawings of a different switch ("Illustrations in this chapter depict the mounting of a DCS-7050QX-32S switch") that carry no measure. The data sheet lists the spares KIT-7001, KIT-2POST-1U-NT, KIT-4POST-NT, KIT-7001-4POST-L and KIT-GND-EXT-1RU. No figure measures a bracket position, and the kit guides are not held, so no ear position is written and no rail kit is listed in chassis.kits. Recorded in the gap rack-ears.

environment.note: Guide Table 2: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -25 to 70 C, altitude 0 to 3,000 m, humidity 5 to 90 percent non-condensing. Data sheet: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -40 to 70 C, humidity 5 to 95 percent, altitude 0 to 3,000 m. Storage temperature and humidity differ: gap `environment`, the guide's used.

front-legend.note: The model legend reads "7280CR3-36S" under the maker's wordmark at the top left (read at 570 px; the print is small). THE WORDMARK IS NOT DRAWN: a logo-zone region is reserved over it and the plain model text is set. The text is as the guide's caption names the model.

front-ports.note: Figure C-5 at 1.2545 px/mm. Thirty-six cages in two stacked rows of eighteen columns (ports 1 to 36). Ports 1 to 32 are sixteen columns in eight two-column blocks: the tab centres read 20.5 and 39.6 mm for the first block, 65.1 for the second, and 352.3 for the last column of the sixteen, a column pitch of 19.0 (the registry's ganged-QSFP pitch) inside a block and 6.5 mm more between blocks. Ports 33 and 34 and ports 35 and 36 are two further columns, centred 378.3 and 398.0 mm. The rows read from the tabs at 18.1 and 31.4 mm down, a row pitch of 13.3. THE CAGE TYPES ARE PARTLY ESTIMATED: the data sheet says "28 x QSFP100, 6 x QSFP200, 2 x QSFP-DD" and no document says which ports are which. Ports 1 to 34 are drawn as the library's ganged QSFP cage (identical opening for QSFP100 and QSFP200), and ports 35 and 36, the two drawn at the right end with an orange legend strip above them, as QSFP-DD cages. The belly-to-belly orientation is the library's convention (upper cage upright, lower turned 180); the figure is too small to show the latch side. Recorded in the gap cage-types.

fru-bays.note: Guide Appendix E (E.2 power supplies, E.3 fan modules) gives removal and installation procedures, and the data sheet calls the supplies "1+1 hot-swappable" and the fans "hot-swap". SO THE TWO POWER SUPPLIES AND THE TWO FAN MODULES ARE BAYS. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit. The management ports are part of the chassis and are placements on the front.

gate-1-front.note: Figure C-5 passes. The raster is 570 x 138 pixels; the body measures 552 px wide and 55 px tall (aspect 10.0), against the data sheet's 440.0 / 43.7 = 10.07, so the figure is near-orthographic and carries geometry at 1.2545 px/mm (the 440 mm body is the scale anchor, its left edge read at 1 px). One pixel is 0.8 mm, so every position is good to about 0.8 mm, and every one is `estimated` because it is read off a picture and no dimension states it. The cage columns were read from the white port-number tabs in a three-times enlargement and the right end in a twelve-times one.

gate-1-rear.note: Figure D-1 is a 553 x 141 px raster whose chassis is 551 px between its edges and 54 px tall (aspect 10.2 against 10.07), 1.252 px/mm over the 440 mm body; positions are good to about 0.8 mm. The guide draws the rear generically (D-1 to D-4) and does not say which model uses which. The 7280CR3-36S is mapped to D-1 by its two fan modules (data sheet: "Hot-swappable Fans 2 (1+1 redundant)"), its 1RU height and its two power supplies. THE MAPPING IS ESTIMATED. Its management ports are on the front (Figure C-5 callouts 6 to 8), so the rear's management block of D-1 is left out: the plate is blank where D-1 draws the block.

interface-names.note: Not printed and not modelled. EOS names ports Ethernet1 to Ethernet36 and Management1; this is the vendor's convention and no held document prints it.

lifecycle.note: Searched 2026-10-23 (web searches of Arista's end-of-sale notices). Notice 23790, "End of Sale of the Arista DCS-7280CR3K-36S Series" (https://www.arista.com/en/support/advisories-notices/end-of-sale/23790-end-of-sale-of-the-arista-dcs-7280cr3k-36s-series), announced April 10, 2026, covers the SKUs -F and # of the 7280CR3K-36S, with the last date to order October 10, 2026, end of life October 10, 2031, and the 7280CR3K-36A as the suggested replacement. It names neither the 7280CR3-36S nor the 7280CR3K-36A, and no notice for those was found, so the device records the announcement and this note says which build it covers: the k-f build only.

management-ports.note: Figure C-5 callouts 6 to 8: the Ethernet management port (top), the USB port (middle) and the console port (serial, bottom), stacked at the right end of the front in a dark dotted frame 417.0 to 434.3 mm across and 5.7 to 38.5 mm down. Placed as the library places the 7280CR3-32D4's rear stack. The small symbols left of each port (arrows, a USB trident, a console symbol) are not legible at this size and are not drawn.

other-faces.note: No source draws the top, bottom or sides flat. The guide's installation figures are isometric. Each carries an `empty` sentence. The 1RU grounding point is on the bottom of the chassis (guide section 4.2, Table 5, KIT-GND-EXT-1RU); no figure measures it.

port-lamps.note: NOT MODELLED. Figure C-5 callout 10, "Port Status LED", points at a mark at the lower right of port 8's cage that the 570 px raster does not resolve into a lamp, and no lamp shows beside any other port. Guide Appendix A.1.2, Table 10 gives the states (off link down, green link up, yellow software disabled, flashing yellow failed diagnostics). Recorded in the gap port-lamps.

port-numbering.note: Figure C-5 (callout 1, "Port numbers") prints 1 over 2, 3 over 4, and so on down each column, 1 to 36 from the left, the odd number on the upper cage. The figure prints each number twice: on a white tab over the cage opening, and small in the lavender strip above the upper cage (odd) and below the lower cage (even). A seated cage hides the tab, so the model prints the strip numerals: the odd numbers above the upper cages and the even numbers below the lower ones. EOS interface names are not printed on the metal and are not modelled.

power.note: Guide Table 4: typical / maximum 254 W / 423 W for the 7280CR3-36S and 7280CR3K-36S, and 262 W / 437 W for the 7280CR3K-36A, each with PWR-1011-AC or PWR-1011-DC. The data sheet states the same figures with typical "measured at 25C ambient with 50% load on all ports". A configuration cannot state a device attribute, so the device carries 254 W / 423 W and the -36A figure is in the gap config-scoped-device-attrs and in the description of its configurations.

rear.note: Figure D-1 at 1.252 px/mm, the rear seen from behind with x = 0 at the left of the drawing. PS1 is the left and PS2 the right (callouts 1 and 6). Each power supply module is 73.5 mm wide (the data sheet's "73.5MM") at 4.4 and 361.5 mm across and 1.85 mm down. Two fan modules 78.6 mm wide at 105.7 and 276.6 mm across and 2.55 mm down. Between the fans is a grey plate printed with ASSY NUMBER, SERIAL NUMBER and MAC ADDRESS fields and, under them, PS1 and PS2 legends beside airflow arrows (the arrows are not drawn).

rear-fan.note: Data sheet: "Hot-swappable Fans 2 (1+1 redundant)"; the front-to-rear fan is "FAN-7011M-F" and the rear-to-front fan "FAN-7011H-R" (a different grade: "Fan Tray: Forward Airflow: FAN-7011M-F, Reverse Airflow: FAN-7011H-R"). Data sheet note 4: rear-to-front airflow "is subject to 35C max ambient temperature and transceiver power restrictions, requires EOS 4.29.1 and High Speed fans (FAN-7011H-R)". Guide section 2.1: a red handle is an air-exit module and a blue handle an air-inlet one. The two fan modules are bays that accept the FAN-7011M-F or the FAN-7011H-R.

sources.note: 7280R3 Series Quick Start Guide, Arista Networks, document DOC-07041-01, 63 pages, PDF created 2025-05-16 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/qsg/qsg-books/QS_7280R3.pdf): Table 1 (dimensions and weights), Table 2 (operating and storage), Table 3 (power input), Table 4 (power draw and supported supplies), section 2.1 (airflow orientation, handle colour), Table 5 (grounding), section 4.5 (serial and management cables), Appendix A (status indicators, Tables 9 to 13), Appendix C (Figure C-5, the front panel of the DCS-7280CR3-36S, 7280CR3K-36S and 7280CR3K-36A), Appendix D (Figure D-1, the rear panel with two fan modules), Appendix E (field replacement). 7280R3 Series Data Center Switch Router Data Sheet, Arista Networks, 03-0045-59, dated August 11th, 2025 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/Datasheets/7280R3-Data-Sheet.pdf): the model comparison of the 7280CR3-36S, CR3K-36S and CR3K-36A, the power supply specifications and the ordering information. The 2022 7280 1RU Gen 3 guide (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/qsg/qsg-books/QS_7280_1RU_Gen3.pdf) lists the 7280CR3-36S in its tables and has no figure for it, so Figure C-5 has no second reading. Held and checked first: intake COVERAGE.md and SOURCES.md, which list no photograph, Visio stencil, 3D model or CAD file for this model (Arista publishes none; the stencil zip could not be fetched). The data sheet's picture of the face is a thumbnail. No drawing, photograph or logo is copied into the library, only transcribed facts and new drawings.

speed-strips.note: Guide Figure C-5 callout 9, "Port Speed Groups": lavender strips above and below each two-column block of ports 1 to 24 and light-blue and lavender strips over ports 25 to 34 and an orange strip at ports 35 and 36, with tiny legends. The strips of ports 1 to 32 are drawn lavender, with the printed numerals above; the colour differences and the legends are not drawn.

status-lamps.note: Guide Appendix A.1.1, Table 9 and Figure C-5 callouts 2 to 5: a system status lamp (blinking green on power-up, green normal, blue locator, amber for two or more failed fans), a fan status lamp (green, amber for one module removed or failed, red for two or more) and a status lamp for each of the two power supplies (green operating, off removed or faulty). Four lamps in a horizontal row at 418.6, 423.3, 427.9 and 432.6 mm and 1.5 mm down, above the management block, with a symbol under each read in a twelve-times enlargement: a circled mark, a fan, and two wave marks for the supplies.

vents.note: The figure shows a perforated grid along the top (0.6 to 9.5 mm down, 27 to 405 mm across) and a ribbed strip along the bottom lip. Two brass-coloured screw heads sit on the lip at 141.9 and 275.2 mm. Each is drawn in its measured extent; the individual squares are not drawn one by one.
